topics.name: Python Reference Implementation Boundary
topics.purpose: Define Python implementation guidance as one reference implementation of canonical toolchain semantics, not the universal semantic truth.

semantics.semantic_rule: Canonical contracts define language-independent required behavior.
semantics.implementation_rule: Python modules/classes/functions may realize those semantics.
semantics.portability_rule: Other languages may implement equivalent behavior.
semantics.authority_rule: Python-specific architecture cannot redefine canonical semantics.
semantics.version_rule: Supported Python runtime/dependencies are explicit in implementation profile.

invariants.rule: Toolchain code, scans, indexes, reports and generated artifacts remain implementation/evidence surfaces; they never become canonical semantic authority unless an explicit accepted canonical definition says so.
Every toolchain execution binds exact bootstrap/source/profile/input revisions and must not resolve ambiguity through filesystem order, newest-wins, mtime, fuzzy names or UI layout.

hard_gates.condition: Python-only concept becomes universal identity silently
